chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.html:
A Chrysos Heir meets him at the border of Okhema. She's to be his guide, yet Mydei can't help but find himself discomfited when he lays eyes on her. She has gray hair and golden eyes. Mydei stares at her and can not seem to figure out what is wrong with the image in front of him. She stares right back for a few silent moments, before finally introducing herself.

"You can call me Stelle," She says. Her gaze is still roaming all over Mydei's figure. Mydei fights the urge to glare at her for her ogling. "It's a pleasure to meet you, your highness." She makes a face at the address. Mydei doesn't comment on it; he can't risk Okhema's ire when he is the one on their doorstep begging for sanctuary.

"Lady Aglaea and Lady Cerydra are waiting for you." Stelle continues. "I'll lead you to them." She doesn't wait for Mydei's response, on swiftly spinning around on her heels and wandering off into the city.

She leads him to the rest of the Chrysos heirs. Lady Cerydra and Aglaea run through the treaties with him easily enough; Stelle takes a backseat from the politics, but Mydei can feel her gaze on him the entire meeting. That pink-haired companion of hers isn't much different.

"Don't mind her too much." Lady Aglaea says. She's wandered closer to Mydei than any of the other heirs. "It's very likely her first time seeing a soldier from Castrum Kremnos."

Mydei blinks. The wars between Castrum Kremnos and Okhema are practically infamous. Nevermind the fact that Castrum Kremnos was a nomadic city to begin.

"How?" To have never encountered a Kremnoan warrior…

"Her hometown is a small, isolated, village," Aglaea says. She pins Mydei with an assessing look, then says. "Aedes Elysiae. I don't know if you've heard of it."

Mydei blinks. He doesn't recognize it, not really. He certainly has no idea where the village is, nor does he know anyone who hails from the place, but something about the name of that village is achingly familiar.

"I don't think so, no." Mydei says, ignoring the strange storm of feelings lashing out in his chest. "Is it customary for people there to introduce themselves and then immediately wander off?"

Aglaea lets out a sigh. "No. But Stelle has her own… quirks. I wouldn't take it to heart. If she has an issue with you she'll say it to your face."

The staring doesn't let up for another week, even after the treaty is finally set and Mydei gets his people somewhat settled into Okhema proper. For what seems like every second of her spare time, Stelle tails after Mydei. Mydei goes grocery shopping- Stelle is hiding behind a planter. Mydei goes to spar in the training grounds- Stelle is hiding behind a dummy.

The fifth time that week, when Mydei spots Stelle hiding behind a large vase by the baths, peeping on him, he snaps.

"Would you stop that?" He hisses out. "What do you even want?" Stelle shrinks behind the amphora, as if trying to make herself smaller. Mydei continues glaring her. She eventually slumps, and finally comes out from behind her hiding place.

"I just wanted to see how you were doing." She says sulkily.

Mydei raises an eyebrow. "And that involves stalking me?"

Stelle mutters under her breath. "I wasn't that bad…" Mydei ignores it. She really was that bad. The only thing that would've made Stelle's hiding even more unsubtle would've been if she'd knocked over that vase while ducking behind it.

"So?"

Stelle pouts. "You're a cool person." She fidgets back and forth. "I really did want to check on how you were doing." She wrinkles up her nose and sticks her tongue out the corner of her mouth in a particularly childish rendition of a 'thinking face'.

"You could have just asked."

"Would you have answered?" Stelle tilts her head like a dog. "Truthfully, I mean." Mydei narrows his eyes at Stelle.

Stelle lets out a sigh. She raises an arm to muss up her own hair. "I just- fffff." She turns her gaze up to the sky. "Leader-types like you? They've got to keep up a strong image for the sake of their people, and all that." She looks back down again. "And as far as I can tell you don't have that many friends-" Mydei bristles "-of equal standing to you, so I figured I'd be the one doing the welfare checks."

"You do not have to." Mydei says. "We barely even know each other."

Stelle's expression falls suddenly. Her gaze brushes back over to Mydei. "Yeah. Right." Her voice has suddenly taken on a sort of hollow quality to it. Mydei can't understand it.

Stelle suddenly shakes herself off. That solemn expression suddenly lifts, and she's back to her usual goofy self. "Let's just say that you remind me of an old friend, yeah? Besides, we're both outsiders. Sue me for being concerned for a fellow outlander."

Mydei doesn't bother correcting Stelle. An outlander from a small, no-name, village is vastly different from an outlander hailing from the infamous Castrum Kremnos. But Stelle's expression is still tight at the edges; perhaps Mydei really does remind her of an old friend she'd lost.

"I really am doing alright." Mydei finally says. "But please stop following me places. Ask me verbally next time, alright?"

Stelle bursts out laughing. She tosses him a thumbs-up. "Sure thing. So long as you make sure to answer back." Mydei awkwardly mirrors her as he nods. Stelle laughs even harder.

"This is Demetria's shop." ███████ motions to the small shop before them. Mydei peers over his guide's shoulder. The ingredients laid out are all fresh; Mydei hasn't seen such high quality ingredients since- well, ever, really.

"I'm not much of a cook." The young man laughs. Mydei glances up towards him. The prince can't see his guide's face. "But I can confidently tell you Demetria's shop is the best place to get your groceries."

Mydei hums. ███████ certainly has an eye for good ingredients, if nothing else.

"If we get the chance, I can make something for you and the other heirs." Mydei offers.

"Would you?" ███████ perks up. Mydei can practically see the tail wagging behind him.

"When we all have the time, perhaps." Mydei responds easily. ███████ makes a happy noise in answer.

"I'll really have to show you around properly, now." ███████ says happily. "As a pre-payment, of course." The young man takes Mydei by the arm and yanks him off away from the vegetable stand. ███████ 's hand is warm against Mydei's skin. Mydei can feel the sword callouses on the other man's palm.

Mydei doesn't do something as undignified as squawk, but it's a near thing. A strangled noise makes its way out of his throat anyway.

"Ah, sorry!" ███████ hurriedly releases Mydei's arm. "Sorry. I've been told I have no sense of personal space…" He laughs nervously, bringing a hand up to run fingers through his hair.

Mydei lets out a breath. "It's alright." He hopes that his blush isn't visible like this. It's been a very long time since anyone has granted him such casual physical touch. The Kremnoans all view him as their prince; their gazes are filled with with awe or contempt- but all find him far too imposing to draw close too. And Mydei's friends…

Mydei shakes off that thought. There's no point in dwelling on the past like that now.

███████ laughs nervously in response. "Still, let me know if you don't like me getting all up in your space, okay? I don't want to make you uncomfortable."

"I will." Mydei says easily.

███████ breaks out into a blinding grin again. This time, when he reaches forward to take Mydei's arm, he makes direct eye contact with Mydei. Mydei offers his arm out; when he's dragged off this time, he only lets out a small huff. He still shivers a bit at the touch, but it's a pleasant feeling, allowing someone to be this close.

"This is Theodoros' shop." ███████ points over to small pottery shop. "He's got really pretty amphoras. I'm personally a collector." ███████ sticks his nose up in the air, puffing up a bit in pride. Mydei snorts.

"The forges are just down the steps." ███████ motions down to the aforementioned forges. Mydei can hear the clang of hammers even this far into the market. "If you ever need anything repaired or made, that where to go. Chartonus is a deft hand at his work."

███████ continues rambling on, motioning to various sights around the city. All along, he enver releases his grip of Mydei's arm. Mydei doesn't try to pull away either; he's content to let ███████ drag him around the city.

By the time their tour wraps up, it is already well into parting hour.

"Ah, I didn't ask." ███████ spins around on his heels. "Where are you staying? I can take you there."

"With the rest of the Kremnoan detachment." Mydei says easily. "It's quite alright. I find my way back."

"No, no," ███████ waves a hand down at Mydei. "It'd be rude for me to just leave you here like this. You're new to Okhema. It's my turn to play the host." ███████ puffs up. He leads Mydei through the streets of Okhema.

Mydei narrows his eyes at ███████, but keeps his mouth shut. ███████ probably didn't mean it in a cruel manner- it certainly isn't the first time that ███████ has put his foot in his mouth Mydei's presence.

"Where do you live, then?" Mydei asks. When ███████ stares at him blankly, Mydei adds on, "So that I can repay the favor to you, in the future."

███████ bursts out laughing. "I live with the other heirs." He says. "In the inner city." He pauses, then leans into Mydei's space and bumps shoulders with the prince. The two men begin walking through the city, back towards Mydei's people.

"If you ever want to meet up just to hang out feel free to come find me." ███████ says. "I think you're a pretty cool guy. You're fun to be around." He raises his arms to brace his hands behind his head. "Besides, you're a really strong fighter. Are you good at other stuff too?"

"Other stuff?" Mydei raises an eyebrow.

"Ah, you know what I mean." ███████ laughs nervously. Mydei can see just the faintest of blushes rising up ███████'s neck. "Something like- fishing?"

Mydei snorts. "Then perhaps we can check the next time we meet."

███████ perks right up. "We can?" He pauses, then repeats. "We can!" Mydei watches as ███████ bounces on his toes. A laugh bubbles up out of Mydei's chest.

"We can." Mydei agrees with a smile. They've finally reached the entrance of the area where the Kremonan detachment is housed. Mydei slows to a stop. "I'll see you tomorrow, then."

███████ is silent for a few moment, staring blankly at Mydei. "I- yeah." ███████ strangles out. For some reason, his neck is really red. ███████ coughs into his fist. "See you tomorrow, Mydeimos."

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.html:
Cyrene is pleasant enough to be around; she's a sweet young girl, terribly polite, and just a generally nice person. Mydei finds himself often avoiding her, anyway.

She has the same sense of whimsical humor as Stelle, but something about her always makes Mydei feel as if she's peeling back his skin with her eyes. She has a strange tendency to disappear into the background, and only really interacts with Stelle. It makes it easier for Mydei to avoid her, but he feels bad about it anyway.

Cyrene seems to recognize how she creeps Mydei out a bit. If it causes her offense, she certainly doesn't show it. Mydei figures he'll probably get used to her solely through sheer exposure. Wherever Stelle goes, Cyrene tends to follow.

The first time Mydei finally gets to have a proper conversation with her alone, it's inside Hyacine's infirmary.

He'd taken one hits too many out on the frontlines. Stelle had been the one to drag his corpse back to Okhema as his body knit itself back together. Now, Mydei lies in an infirmary bed. He's under strict orders by Hyacine to not move. Mydei personally doesn't think it's necessary at all; all his injuries are gone, save for a few internal aches, but those will fix themselves up by the end of the hour.

The only reason he hasn't actually gotten out of bed is because of little Ica, who's perched on Hyacine's desk just across the room. The unicorn is happily munching away on an entire basket of apples, its beady little eyes fixed on Mydei. No doubt, if Mydei so much as dips a toe out of bed, the thing will go flying off to snitch to Hyacine.

Mydei sighs. He flexes his hand. He's terribly bored.

"How are you feeling?" Cyrene stands at the edge of of Mydei's infirmary bed, just outside the curtains.

"Fine." Mydei says. Cyrene blinks at him, clearly not believing his words. He's well aware of the number of bandages Hyacine had insistently wrapped around him, despite his wounds having already closed with his resurrection. It certainly isn't helping his claim.

Cyrene hums. She's smiling softly at Mydei, but she's staring blankly at Mydei again. There's a strange combination of warm fluffiness and ghostly distance mixed in her expression. "I'm glad you're okay." She says.

Mydei blinks. "Thank you?" He's more confused than anything. He hasn't interacted with Cyrene much at all, save for a few cursory glances. She's never made any indication of wanting to interact with Mydei either. Yet she's standing at Mydei's bedside wishing him well…

"I like stories with happy endings." Cyrene says. She rocks back and forth on her feet, her hands folded behind her back.

"Just say what you wish to say." Mydei says. He winces; the words sound harsh even to his ears. Cyrene, though, laughs, lightly and softly like a set of jingle bells. For a moment, Mydei feels as if Cyrene is the one who had just died, a ghost floating lightly back from the Sea.

"I like stories with happy endings." Cyrene repeats. "And we finally have a chance to change our ending." She smiles smally. "I probably won't be able to see it, so I hope that you can see it in my place."

"Pardon?" Mydei furrows his brow in confusion. "I- thank you, but I didn't think we were that close?" Friendly, perhaps, but certainly not close enough to make lifelong promises to one another.

Cyrene's still swaying back and forth. "There's someone at the very end, waiting for both of us to come back." Cyrene continues on. "I don't want to disappoint him, but I really don't think I'll make it. So at the very least, you should make it to the end."

"To Era Nova?" Cyrene's not making any sense at all. Mydei wants to pry, but Cyrene's eyes have gained a glazed look to them, almost as if she isn't entirely present. She stares at Mydei, yet she's staring right past him.

"If you'd like to think of it like that. A real Era Nova." Cyrene starts giggling to herself. She covers her smile with her hands as her shoulders shake with her laughter. Mydei stares at her, dumbfounded.

When Cyrene's laughter finally dies down, she leans forward and clasps Mydei's hand in hers. "Could you just make me this one little promise, then? To survive until the very end?"

Mydei stares at her. Molten orange meets deep blue. The shade of blue is off. It's too dark.

"I will do all I can for the Flamechase Journey." Mydei finally says.

Cyrene squeezes Mydei's hand. "Mydei, that's not what I asked for." Her smile turns pained. "Can you promise me to live? Even if not for me, then for all the people who love you."

Mydei stares at her silently. There's still blood on his skin, and aches in his bones and flesh from his last death.

"Alright." He finally says, if only to satisfy Cyrene. Cyrene's eyes glance over Mydei's expression, searching. Mydei casts his expression down into it's usual stony mein. Cyrene seems to find something, though, because when her eye's meet Mydei's, a laugh bubbles out of her throat.

She laughs loudly and heartily, nothing like the light, ghostly giggles Myde is used to hearing from her.

"I think you're a great person, Mydeimos." She finally releases Mydei's hand. "I've liked you since the very first time we met. And the two of you did always complement each other so well." She takes a step away from Mydei's bedside.

"The two of who?" Mydei asks. "Stelle and me?"

Cyrene holds up a finger to her cheek and tilts her head. "Maybe?" She starts giggling again. "If you remember, you'll remember. I'm sure you'll figure it out one day." She spins on her heels and skips out of the infirmary.

Mydei watches her leave.

Many of the things in Okhema are foreign to Mydei. Small things, like their taste in food and taste in dress. Larger things, like the long stretches of peacetime, the happy people in the streets, the bright sun overhead. The majority of these things, he finds that he doesn't think he will ever be tired of.

The chimeras are also a new experience. They fall under the category of small things. They're small, fluffy and adorable little creatures, who are always happy to grab food from between Mydei's fingers. The prince finds himself visiting the Garden of Life quite often in his free time. Today, ███████ accompanies him.

███████ holds up the orange chimera by its armpits. He sticks his face far too close to the chimera. The chimera lets out a little awoo.

"That one's name is Fig Stew." Mydei says.

A gray chimera lets out a loud mewl and starts clawing at ███████'s stomach, trying to climb up his torso. Mydei reaches forward to pull the gray chimera into his arms. It keeps on fussing, waving its little paws in the direction of its friend.

"This one is Beagle Coconut." Mydei holds the gray chimera up to his eyeline. It yowls.

"He's a fussy little guy." ███████ laughs. He lowers Fig Stew into his lap, and the orange chimera curls up, tucking its nose under its tail. Beagle Coconut squirms and squirms. Mydei finally lowers the chimera down to the ground, and it goes running straight for Fig Stew.

Fig Stew blinks blearily when Beagle Coconut launches itself at it. Both chimeras go tumbling out of ███████'s lap with a squeak when Beagle Coconut makes contact.

███████ laughs and shifts so that he isn't at risk at crushing the creatures. Mydei watches ███████'s expression, just a little bit awestruck. There's something beautiful about ███████, even though Mydei can't ever quite see his face. The sun falls warmly down on ███████'s hair. ███████'s smile would surely be stunning. Perhaps it is ███████'s soul that is beautiful.

"Mydei?"

Mydei snaps out of his thoughts. He blinks dumbly at ███████. "What?"

"You were zoning out." ███████ leans forward, propping his chin on his hands. Mydei thinks ███████ is winking at him. "Were you admiring me? Am I that beautiful?" ███████ teases.

Mydei scowls. He can feel his ears burning; hopefully the flush doesn't show on the rest of his face. "Who's admiring who? I'm just looking at the chimeras."

"It's okay." ███████ laughs. "I know I'm handsome. I'll let you look all you want if you let me do the same in turn." He tips his head to the side, probably fluttering his eyelashes.

Mydei makes a strangled noise. The blush has spread down to his shoulders; there is no way that his flustered state isn't obvious to the other party.

Mydei stubbornly turns his gaze down to the two chimeras. Beagle Coconut and Fig Stew have curled up together in the grass between them. Fig Stew is curled up, this time finally having obtained its desired nap. Beagle Coconut, on the other hand, is chewing on Fig Stew's tail.

Mydei reaches forward to gently free Fig Stew from Beagle Coconut's grasp. Beagle Coconut whines, but scooches itself up along to grass to plaster itself against Fig Stew's back.

"They really are quite adorable, don't you think?" ███████ says. Mydei glances up at him. ███████ continues. "A pity that we can't take any home with us." He leans in far too close to the chimeras for Mydei's comfort.

"Don't."

"Who's gonna stop me?"

"Hyacine." Mydei says drily. "Lady Aglaea. Lady Tribios. The Garden manager. Me"

███████'s shoulder slump. "Killjoy." He whines. He lets out a small sigh. "Maybe one day I'll be able to get a dog again…" The last part is mumbled under his breath. Mydei doesn't think he was supposed to hear it.

"Leave the poor chimeras alone." Mydei says instead. "You're starting to look like Beagle Coconut with all this pouting."

"But aren't they so cute?" ███████ whines, proving Mydei's exact point. Mydei turns his head away, even as a smile quirks up the corners of his lips.

"If you really want a pet, maybe we can find a pet cat, or something similar." Mydei offers.

███████ whips his head around to face Mydei so quickly that Mydei is surprised it doesn't give ███████ whiplash. ███████ faces Mydei for a few silent moments, before asking, "Do you want a pet cat?"

Mydei blinks. "I am in no position to be taking care of a pet."

"Well, hypothetically, then." ███████ says. "When this is all over, would you like a pet cat?"

"…Perhaps." They're elegant creatures, certainly, and Mydei is always happy to stop and feed the street cats.

███████ nods once. "Then, some day in the future, we can get some pet cats."

"We?"

███████ laughs. "Of course. What, do you want to care for them all by yourself." Mydei sniffs, but doesn't respond.

"Some day in the future." ███████ repeats quietly, sitting upright. "We'll get a pet cat. And maybe a pet dog. And we can just laze around and eat and sleep and not have to worry about anything." He stares down at the chimeras. Beagle Coconut has fallen asleep too, and is happily basking in the sun alongside Fig Stew.

Mydei looks away. The two chimeras are still cuddled together on the grass.

"That's a nice dream." Mydei says.

"Isn't it?" ███████ laughs. "Maybe I'll make it mine."

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.html:
"What was Aedes Elysiae like?" Mydei absently asks.

Stelle blinks up at him, her spoon hanging out of her mouth.

"Wuh?" She stutters, the utensil dropping out from between her lips. "What? Huh?? Stelle blinks some more. "What brought this on?"

Mydei shrugs stiffly. "I was just curious."

Stelle hums, turning back to her food. Mydei had made honeycakes for the heirs again. As usual, the majority of the treat had been scarfed down by Little Ica and Stelle.

"It was really gold." Stelle says. She shrugs again. "I'm not gonna lie, I'm not the best person to ask about it."

"Didn't you grow up there?"

"Not really." Stelle shoves a bite of food into her mouth. "I grew up somewhere else. I didn't move to Aedes Elysiae until just a few months before it was destroyed. I didn't get to stay long at all."

"Oh." It's reasonable for Mydei to be confused; for someone who claims to hail from Aedes Elysiae, Stelle doesn't seem to know the village all that well at all. What's less reasonable is the strange sense of disappointment that's rearing its head in Mydei's chest.

"There were these two baby seals that lived in one of the inlets along the coast." Stelle speaks up. "I remember going there to play with them a lot. They were really cute." She tilts her head to the side. "There was a pink Chimera, too, by the pond Cyrene and I would play at. Cyrene loved the thing."

What about the people? Mydei wants to ask. But he has a feeling that the answers Stelle will give him won't be the ones he's looking for.

Stelle seems to catch onto Mydei's mood. She looks up at him sheepishly. "I'm sorry." She says. "I don't have the stories you're looking for."

"That's alright." Mydei says, even though it kind of isn't.

"What was Castrum Kremnos like?" Stelle asks awkwardly instead. "Or your friends from before that?" Judging by her wince, she's well aware that she's stepping on a potential landmine. Luckily for her, Mydei isn't particularly sensitive about his past.

"Large." Mydei says. "Loud, at its height." He pauses, then adds on. "My friends were loud too. They were loyal. Sociable. I cared for them deeply."

Stelle softens. "I care for my companions too." She leans forward, pushing the last few bites of honeycake around on her plate. "I haven't seen them in a long time. I'm sure they're doing okay, but still." She takes a bite. "It sucks not being able to see them."

Mydei stares at Stelle for a few moments. Then, he says, "You've never lost anyone before, have you."

Stelle stares down at her plate. "Not really." She says. "Not in the same way as you. More than once, I've thought them gone, only for them to return." She takes another bite. "I was lucky."

"You were lucky." Mydei blankly parrots. Then, he says. "You didn't have an entire nation depending on you, either."

Stelle hums. "I respect you greatly, Prince Mydeimos." Stelle says. It's the first time Mydei has heard her address him by his full title. "But I can't understand it. I don't think I ever will. Being a ruler, or anything like that. I'm the kind of person who just happily does whatever they want, without worrying about things like that."

"And yet here you are, playing such a major role in the Flamechase."

Stelle laughs, as if Mydei has just told a particularly funny joke. "That's a fate I willingly took up, too." She leans forward, propping her chin up on the palm of her hand.

"I don't think fate is something that can be picked up willingly." Mydei says. "It simply just is."

"Can't it?" Stelle asks breezily. "We are both here by fate. Your father chose to defy it, and it led to you being here. I chose to embrace it, and here I am. Even if the finale is the same, I still made the choice to come to Okhema for myself." She cleans up the last of the honeycake. "Perhaps we're slightly similar, in that we're both bearing Okhema's fate on our shoulders. But you were carrying Castrum Kremnos' fate all by yourself."

"It can be… tiring." Mydei admits. "But at the end of the day there is no one else to share that burden."

"I wouldn't know." She says quietly. "I've always had my friends by my side."

"And how fortunate you are for that." Mydeimos murmurs.

Stelle's spoon scrapes loudly against the plate. "I'm not a ruler. I am barely even a hero. I don't know how to be, and I don't want to be."

"How fortunate for you." Mydei says drily.

She looks up at Mydei, her lips quirked downward in a slight frown. "I'm a simple traveler. I can not relate to you. I can not comfort you." She sets her spoon down on the plate. "I'm sorry I can't be who you want, or who you're looking for."

Mydei bristles at the accusation, but he doesn't protest. Even he is aware of his tendencies to gravitate towards Stelle. He's not even sure why he does so. The two of them have barely anything in common.

Sometimes, Mydei feels as if he is looking for a ghost, when he looks at Stelle. Perhaps that's why he'd asked her about Aedes Elysiae today; once again, he'd been searching for someone who isn't there.

Stelle stares at him. Her eyes are gold.

They're the wrong color again.

For some reason, they always end up sparring on the rooftops above the Marmoreal Market.

Mydei doesn't think much of it usually; he's far too used to sparring in any sort of open location, having spent the majority of his life on the road. The rooftop of a building isn't much different from a small clearing to him; so long as there is space to move throught footwork and swing a weapon, Mydei is satisfied.

Their spars always go something like this:

███████ barges into Mydei's room at a ridiculously early hour on their day off.

"Let's go to Marmoreal Market!" He crows, all as Mydei is still rubbing sleep out of his eyes. They wander through the market, do their shopping, and inevitably, climb up onto the rooftops. It's usually Mydeimos leading them up there, to be fair. The sky overhead is clear, and the sun is warm on his skin. The rooftops they stand on offers Mydei a fantastic view of Okhema.

"You're like a cat," ███████ teases, "Always ending up in high places."

Mydei sniffs. "Like you aren't happily following me." He shoots back.

"Where would I go if not with you?" ███████ responds, entirely earnest.

Mydei flusters, and in a desperate bid to diffuse whatever tension it is that's building up between them, shoots out with a challenge. "You lost in our last spar. Let's see if you can beat me this time."

███████ laughs, despite the abrupt change in topic.

And so, here they are now, sparring on the rooftops yet again.

███████ lunges at Mydei with a wooden sword. Mydei easily blocks the swing; he swerves around the blade to land his own hit on ███████'s torso. ███████ laughs with the strike connects, and slips into familiar footwork as he twists around Mydei's movements. It's like a well worn dance, these spars between them.

Mydei grins madly as he ducks under another strike; the thrills of their clashes never grows old. Neither have to hold back in order to match the other. It's a fantastic feeling; being able to find someone who can match him so easily. That feeling of being equal- for a prince and a hero, it's a rare, prized, feeling.

Mydei's just ducking another swing when an enraged voice rings out.

"███████! Mydeimos!"

███████ freezes in his steps. He nearly skids off the side of the roof with the momentum. Mydei grabs ███████ by the arm and yanks him back onto the center of the roof. ███████'s entire posture slumps down into something like guilt. Mydei's gauntlet freezes just inches from ███████'s face.

"You two get down here right this instant!" Aglaea barks out. She has her hands propped up on her hips as she glares up at ███████ and Mydei from the ground. Mydei thinks she might be tapping her foot impatiently on the ground, but it's a bit difficult to tell from this height. He shifts his weight from foot to foot and hears one of the roof tiles crack beneath his weight. Ah, yeah. Mydei winces. That would do it.

"Sorry." ███████ whines. He drops down from the roof in a single swift movement. Mydeimos pushes himself down after the swordsman.

"We have perfectly good training grounds." Aglaea seethes. "On the ground. With dirt flooring. Far away from any easily breakable buildings or civilians."

"I'm really sorry." ███████ whines. The full force of Aglaea's wrath seems to be concentrated on him. Mydei swallows down the urge to laugh; he's new enough to Okhema that Lady Aglaea isn't yet as comfortable scolding him, but the last thing he wants is to draw her ire.

"We just forgot." ███████ continues. "We're really sorry." He's really looking like a scolded puppy now; Mydei can practically see the fluffy ears pressed back against ███████'s head.

"Training. Grounds." Agalaea enunciates, pointing a finger in the direction of said training grounds. "This is the third time this week the two of you have caused such a disruption." She swivels here gaze over the Mydei and narrows her eyes. "And you. Don't think your getting out of this scot free either."

"Of course not." Mydei says stiffly. Pauses, then tacks on, "Ma'am." Aglaea's stare only narrows even further. Mydei keeps his expression still as he stares right into Aglaea's eyes.

Eventaully, Aglaea lets out a sigh. The fury seems to drain right out of her. "Just don't do it again." She says. "Seriously. You all are disturbing the city folk." She turns her stare down to ███████. "And stop picking fights, ███████."

"But I'm not." ███████ sulks. Mydei elbows him in the side. ███████ shuts up.

Aglaea heaves out an even louder sigh. Mydei feels kind of bad for her, but then again, he's part of the problem.

"Go find Lady Tribios later." Aglaea finally says. "I don't have the energy to deal with you two. She can give you your punishments."

"Yes ma'am," ███████ and Mydei mumble in unison. Both stand stiffly as Lady Aglaea finally treads away. As soon as Aglaea diappears from sight, ███████ slumps forward.

Mydei bumps his shoulder against ███████'s. "Want to go play with the chimera's? Let's see who can get more to follow them around."

███████ perks right back up, a laugh startling out of him. Almost as soon as he does, he deflates again, wincing. "Now?"

Mydei snorts. "Of course not. We both know Lady Aglaea can still see us." He reaches over and grabs ███████ by the elbow. ███████ laughs again.

"We'll go later, then," ███████ leans into Mydei.

chapters.title: Chapter 4
chapters.html:
After that conversation in the infirmary, Cyrene takes to trailing around Mydei almost just as much as she does Stelle. She's still a bit creepy, but she's grown on Mydei, a bit like a fluffy bit of moss. Soft, fuzzy, and largely harmless, if a bit strange to find in the middle of the city.

Cyrene certainly always has interesting stories, and is always happy to help taste test whatever new treats he makes. She's a good listener too, quite content to let Mydei ramble about whatever interest has grabbed ahold of him for the day.

They're in the Garden of Life today. Mydei had decided to visit the chimeras. He'd run into Cyrene just at the base of the elevator, and the young girl had happily tagged along.

"These are my tarot cards." Cyrene says, spreading out the aforementioned cards all along the ground. "They're one of the only things I managed to save from my hometown." She and Mydei sit in the grass. A pair of chimeras- one orange and one gray- clamber into Cyrene's lap. Mydei reaches forward to pull the orange one out. He places it on the ground in front of them, but the orange chimera crawls into Mydei's lap instead.

"They're pretty." Mydei says. Because he has never been a fan of, much less interested in, prophecy; that's far more Lady Tribios's domain. The gray chimera squeaks and runs over to its companion, paws kicking up the tarot cards every which way. It spins around in a circle and plops itself down in Mydei's lap as Cyrene reorganizes her cards. Mydei absently runs a hand over its fur.

Cyrene giggles. "They are pretty." She taps her finger against a red-toned card. "This one is the Ruler. It represents discipline, authority, and glory." Mydei leans forward to get a better look. He raises an eyebrow when he finds his own faceless likeness staring up at him.

"Is that supposed to have my image on it?" He asks. There goes another point in the column for creepy Cyrene.

"All of them do." Cyrene says easily, like it's completely normal for your prophecy tools to have your friends' faces engraved on them. She pulls out another card. "This one is the Scholar." Professor Anaxagoras stares up at Mydei. "And the Weaver." This time it's Lady Aglaea.

She lays out the rest of her cards. Every single one of them features the likeness of the Heirs.

"Where's Stelle?" Mydei asks, once Cyrene has set all her cards out in front of them. The orange chimera has pressed up against Cyrene's side; it props its little head up on Cyrene's leg, and is happily snoring away.

Cyrene falls silent for a moment. Then, she reaches into her coat and pulls out the last tarot card from an inner pocket.

"This card is the card for the Deliverer." Cyrene slowly slides the card towards Mydei. This figure, for once, is not that of one of the Chrysos Heirs. It's a young man wielding a broadsword. He has white hair, and is dressed in a long white coat. The card itself is painted in shades of deep blue.

"Deliverer." It's flows familiarly off of Mydei's tongue. It scrapes his throat on the way up.

"He's a very important person to me." Cyrene says. "He's family."

"Deliverer." Mydei repeats. There's something in his throat. His heart is clenched in a vice. Mydei reaches a hand forward to run fingertips over the textured surface of the card. He suddenly feels the strange urge to cry.

Twelve cards. Twelve heirs of the Flame Chase. Stelle's visage is not here amongst these painted figures. There is a terribly familiar white-haired man instead.

"The Deliverer." Mydei says. "Is supposed to represent the Worldbearing." It's not a question. Cyrene doesn't correct him.

"Stelle is the heir of the worldbearing." Mydei continues. Those words feel wrong on his tongue, like he's telling a lie. "But she isn't here." He picks up the Deliverer card between his finger tips. He holds the flimsy card up, between his and Cyrene's faces.

"Who is this, then?" The card shakes in front of Mydei's vision. Mydei realizes his hand is the one that's trembling. He lowers the card back to the ground. The motion gives him a clear view of Cyrene's expression.

She's still smiling in that floaty way of hers. But like that time in the infirmary, she looks strangely sad. She briefly closes her eyes and she reaches forward and pushes the tarot card towards Mydei.

"I think you should have it."

Mydei chokes on what he thinks might be a sob. "You just said that these were all you had of your homeland."

"I still have the other cards." Cyrene says easily. "And I still have my memories." She taps the card with her fingernail. "No, it's much more important for you to have this.

She tips her head to the side and picks up the card. Taking Mydei's hand, she presses the card into his palm.

"I miss him a lot." Cyrene says, as she curls Mydei's fingers around the card. "But I have my memories of him. You don't, even though you're still missing him terribly. So you should have this. Maybe it'll help you remember."

"Remember who, Cyrene?" Mydei chest aches. There's a gaping hole in his life that's been there ever since he'd set foot in Okhema. He's always turning to face a ghost and there's a name just on the tip of his tongue that he can no longer recall. "Who am I trying to remember?"

Cyrene just smiles sadly.

Sometimes, they stop at old ruins simply to admire the view.

Mydei's relationship with the night is complicated. The Black Tide is practicaly synonymous with the night time, these days, and it is nothing if not a horror. Castrum Kremnos, though, back when it stood, had followed those a day-night cycle. He'd loved the stars, in those days. It'd been a freeing feeling, watching those small, pretty patches of light glitter overhead from his mother's lap. She'd point out constellations for him and recite their stories, and Mydei had loved it.

After the black tide, though, when the sun stopped shining at all-

Okhema is bathed in eternal sunlight. Even at curtain-fall hour, the Dawn Device still lights up the sky as if it is mid-day. Mydei can not see the stars at all, within Okhema's walls. Mydei can not see the stars on the outside, either, in the places where the black tide has consumed the land.

The particular spot that he and ███████ have camped out today is one of the few spots left, outside of Okhema's walls, that is yet untouched by the Black Tide. Like this, Mydeimos can still see the stars. He stares up at the cosmos, ███████ by his side.

"Castrum Kremnos had a massive library." Mydei says. He's feeling nostalgic, seeing the stars like this. He'd gone stargazing once, back when his friends had still lived. It'd been a sight not unlike this one. "I practically spent my entire childhood in there. It was easy to get lost in between the shelves; not even my father could find me sometimes." They're laying on the roof of a temple in Janusopolis, hanging their legs off over the edge. It's a well deserved break from the hours of fighting they'd just trudged through.

" Aedes Elysiae was a tiny village." ███████ responds in turn. " The only books we had were a few storybooks, and the textbooks in the schoolhouse." Some of the lights in Janusopolis have yet to go out. Their little perch on the roof is illuminated by the dim blue light of old lanterns.

"The city itself was a mobile city." Mydei says. "Sometimes you'd wake in the morning to an ocean view, and by the evening you'd be in a desert." The air out here is cold, almost bitingly so, but it's refreshing on Mydei's heated skin.

"We had wheat fields for as far as the eye could see." ███████ continues. "We'd make a game of hiding in the stalks and seeing who could find the other the fastest." He lets out a small breath; it clouds in the cold night.

"I didn't have that many friends growing up." Mydei tips his head towards ███████. "My mother would often tell me stories instead. She was my only friend in my childhood." The light of the night illuminates ███████'s figure. Mydei finds himself staring at ███████, enraptured.

"I liked fishing at the pier." ███████ turns over onto his side to face Mydei. Mydei can't look away.

Castrum Kremnos was my home. Mydei doesn't say. Because it hadn't been, not really. It'd been his mother within it, then her people after her death. Never the imposing buildings, or the cold, sharp-edged streets, all stained with the memory of his father.

"We had a pet dog named Snowy." ███████ says quietly. "Both of my parents worked in the fields. Cyrene and I were just about to leave for the outside world to study." He reaches towards Mydei and brushes a lock of hair out of the prince's face. ███████'s hand trembles with the movement. Mydei has the sudden urge to take ███████'s hand in his own, so he does.

"There was this lake that Cyrene and I would always play by," ███████ continues, as Mydei rubs circles into ███████ 's palm with his thumb. "She'd read her tarot cards to me. We'd go and play with the fairies in the forest.

"Aedes Elysiae was my home." ███████ chokes out. Mydei reaches forward. He cups ███████'s face with his other hand. ███████ leans into the touch as Mydei runs a thumb over his cheekbone. ███████ clasps his hand over Mydei's.

"It sounds beautiful." Mydei whispers.

"It was." ███████ says quietly. "It really was." He curls forward, leaning into Mydei's space. Mydei reaches forward, bringing up an arm to loop over ███████'s torso.

"I'm a little jealous," ███████ mumbles, "That you still have a history to protect. He leans forward, pressing his forehead against Mydei's. His hand comes up to wrap around the back of Mydei's neck. "That you still have family left to protect."

"You're my family." Mydei blurts. "And the rest of the heirs. Okhema. We both have them."

███████ pauses. "You're right." He mumbles. His nose is brushing Mydei's. They're pressed closely together. Mydei feels terribly warm and bitingly cold at the same time. This affection, so freely given- Mydei could get drunk off of it. Yet ███████ sounds as if he is on the verge of tears, and Mydei hates it with every fiber of his being.

███████ tips his head and pulls away. His hand is still resting on the back of Mydei's neck.

"Thank you," ███████ says. His voice is tinged with melancholy, and Mydei crush that pain beneath his boots. "I think of you as family as well. I'd like to be able to protect you too." His words slur. He sounds exhausted.

"I just miss them, that's all." ███████ says. He tips forward again, pressing his forehead into Mydei's shoulder. Mydei doesn't know what to say; he settles for pulling ███████ into a hug.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 5
chapters.html:
Like any soldier worthy of bearing the title of Strife, Mydei is a seasoned fighter, and often quite happy to throw himself into combat on Okhema's behalf. The Black Tide hasn't been getting any better over the last few years, though it doesn't seem to be spreading as quickly either. They no longer have to fear the Black Tide suddenly swallowing Okhema, but regular border controls and clean-ups are still required.

Mydei and Stelle had been sent out one such mission- nothing too difficult, just clearing out one of the borders of Okhema. The fight's practically routine- to the point that Mydei finds himself slipping into old patterns. The thrill of the fight is getting to him, a little bit. There's adrenaline rushing in his veins. There's something almost like joy pounding through his heart.

A bolt flashes past Mydei's head, only barely missing his head. It nails the corrupted creature just ahead of Mydei; the creature crumples to the ground at Mydei's feet.

Mydei twists around, just about to scold ███████.

"Deliverer-" The name flows easily off his tongue.

Stelle turns to him with a wide-eyed stare. Mydei freezes. ███████ is not here. ███████ has never been here.

"Mydei?" Stelle's expression is twisted up in surprised confusion.

"That's not your name." Mydei manages to choke out.

Stelle swings her bat, taking out the black-tide monster that'd been rushing her. "Mydei," She hisses, and she dashes towards him. Mydei realizes too late that he's left his back open. He flinches to the side as Stelle blocks a strike for him.

"Focus, goddammit." She bites out at him. There's frenzy in her eyes as she shoves past Mydei to lash out at another monster.

Who is ███████? Mydei wants to ask. There's a lump in his throat. The name is just on the tip of his tongue. Yet no matter how hard he thinks, he can not recall it. But there's still a battle roaring around him, and Mydei's a seasoned warrior; he knows how to prioritize. So he shoves back the confusing mess of hurt and longing and anger right back down and turns to focus on the fight.

When the last monster falls at Mydei's feet, Stelle turns to to Mydei.

"You called me Deliverer." She says quietly. She stares up at Mydei. Her gaze is a piercing gold; Mydei feels as if she's peeling him apart. "Why do you know that name?"

"Cyrene told me." Mydei answers, even though that's only half of the truth. There's a storm of emotions welling up behind his ribs. Longing, hurt, anger, pain and something that tastes like love all at once. He can recognize it as missing someone, but he doesn't know who he's missing. There's a strange empty space right by his side, and Mydei finds himself wanting to turn to it. "There's a tarot card for the Deliverer."

Stelle's eyes widen minutely. Then, her expression furrows, and she takes a small step back. "Cyrene?"

"The pink-haired girl who's always following you around." Mydei says. He looks away from Stelle. He doesn't want to look at her right now. "Surely you know her?"

"I-" Stelle blinks. "Yes. I do." The frenzy melts from her eyes, twisting into something like bitter confusion. "She told you his title." Stelle finally parrots blankly.

"Yes?" Mydei ignores Stelle's strange reaction. He doesn't mention how it hadn't been entirely because of Cyrene. The name Deliverer is loaded with all sorts of unspoken things, none of it Mydei can decipher. He'd been caught up in the thrill of battle, and turned to call out to an old friend, only to be met with an empty space and the entirely wrong person.

"I- no." Stelle shakes her head. "Don't worry about it. I just didn't think she'd talk to you, is all." Stelle pauses, then adds on. "Did she ever tell you his name."

Mydei is silent for a few moments. Finally, he says, "I think she thought I already knew his name."

"Do you?"

"…no."

Stelle stares at him. There's something like pity in her eyes.

"If you ever talk to Cyrene again…" Stelle starts. "Can you tell me what she says?"

Mydei blinks. "Why?"

"Curiosity." Stelle shrugs. "I didn't think she'd try talking to you." She turns her gaze away and chews on her lower lip. "I haven't seen her talk to anyone in a really long time.

Mydei frowns. "I don't see why not." He says hesitantly. "If she's fine with it."

Stelle nods easily in response. Then, she pauses, and says. "If you get the chance, you should ask her more about the Deliverer." And there's that name again.

"She knew him better than I did." Stelle continues. "If she can, I'm sure she'll be glad to share stories about him with you." She stares at Mydei for a few more moments, then slowly takes a step back.

Mydei can't read Stelle's expression at all. They may be comrades, fellow soldiers in this brutal war, but he can not call her a close friend. She is a trusted companion, certainly but there is always something missing when Mydei looks at her. It's like looking at a painting and finding that the trees in the background are blue. It's not an obvious error at first glance, but the longer you stare, the more jarring it gets.

Mydei looks away again. Stelle's disappeared out of Mydei's line of sight while he'd been lost in thought. He stands in the corner of their camp, terribly alone. There is nothing around him but the black abyss of the night, and the cold breeze and dull stones.

"Deliverer." Mydei tries again. His chest hurts something fierce. The Deliverer is a hero. The Deliverer is a beloved partner. The Deliverer should be at Mydei's side while he fights this terrible war.

The Deliverer is gone. Mydei can't even remember his name anymore, let alone his face. Or rather- perhaps he's only slowly remembering now? But to have forgotten to begin with-

Mydei rubs the heel of his palm against his sternum. "Deliverer." He calls out again.

Whoever that person was, they don't respond.

Stelle and Dan Heng are two outlanders from a land no one has ever heard of. ███████ had been the one to bring them into Okhema. Mydei isn't quite sure what to feel of the outlanders. With the way things have been going, Okhema's become flooded with refugees from all corners of the planet.

"They remind me a bit of you." Mydei comments. He glances at ███████, who stands at his side. They're perched at the edges of the roofs of Marmoreal Market, on the walkway above the forges.

Rather than the usual spar, this time their surveilling the two outlanders instead. Dan Heng stands by the smithy, nervously wringing his hands together as he waits for his spear to be returned to him. Stelle, meanwhile, is flitting about to and fro trying to poke every remotely interesting object she comes across.

"Really?" ███████ laughs. "I don't think so at all." He leans closer to Mydei, hooking his chin on the prince's shoulders.

"Outlanders with a hero complex and unknown origins?" Mydei says dryly. "Really." ███████ laughs some more. Mydei reaches up to cup ███████'s face with his hand.

"Well, I think I can see myself in Stelle, maybe." ███████ says. "All bubbly energy and happy vibes." He glances up towards Mydei and smiles. "Don't you think?"

Mydei snorts and twists his wrist to lightly pinch ███████'s cheek. "Sure." ███████ whines at Mydei's disbelieving tone, but ███████ plasters himself along Mydei's side anyway. He's a solid line of heat against Mydei's body.

"Didn't Aglaea tell you to go show them around?" Mydei asks.

███████ shrugs. "They're handling themselves fine." He presses even closer to Mydei. "I'd rather spend time with you."

Mydei clicks his tongue and looks back down to the two outlanders. He can feel himself blushing. "I'm fairly certain she meant for you to be guarding from them, really."

███████ hums. "I think it'll be okay."

"Oh? And what tells you that?"

███████ laughs. "Intuition, maybe?" He stands upright, finally detaching himself from Mydei.

"This isn't the time to relax." Mydei says, frowning.

"I'm not, don't worry." ███████ laughs. "Didn't you just say that they reminded you of me?"

"I was referring to the idiotic tendency of sticking your nose in every corner." Mydei shoots back, even though he smiles with every word.

███████ laughs brightly and leans in close to Mydei. "I think those outsiders are cool." He says easily. "And I think they might be the change we need to fight the Black Tide."

Mydei lets out a breath. "You know why I'm worried."

"I'm worried too." ███████ says easily. "I'd be a fool not to be. Still, can you trust my instincts this time?" He reaches up and brushes a lock of hair out of Mydei's face. Mydei's eyes flutter close. He leans into ███████'s touch.

An unfamiliar voice suddenly reings out. "Whoa this is really high up."

Mydei's eyes snap back open. He doesn't flinch, but it's a near thing. ███████ has pulled away and spun around on his heels as well.

Mydei's eyes flash past ███████ over to the edge of the walkway.

"Hi," Stelle wiggles her fingers in greeting. "Whatcha guys doin' up here?" The outlander is in the middle of hauling herself up onto the walkway, one leg dangling over the edge, the other hitched up over the railing.

"How did you even climb up here?" ███████ asks, incredulous.

"The smithy roof." Stelle says easily. She hauls her other leg over the railing and drops onto the walkway in a heap. She lazily rolls onto her back and stares up at ███████ and Mydei from the ground.

"I got bored." She says. "Dan Heng's having a nervous fit over Cloud Piercer but he's been like that for hours now. He'll be fine." She rolls over onto her stomach. "Do you guys have anything fun?"

Mydei stares disbelievingly at Stelle. Stelle tips her head to the side like a dog. Titans, she really is a lot like Phainon.

"You could wander around the market…" ███████ offers.

"You told me to stay at the smithy and 'not go anywhere without supervision.'" Stelle makes finger quotes. She glances over at Mydei and purses her lips. "I thought the golden lady wanted you for something. Didn't think you had a date." She blinks, then throws ███████ a thumbs up and a grin. "I mean, go for it bro."

███████ heaves out a sigh. Mydei fights the urge to laugh.

They end up wandering around the lower levels of the Marmoreal market. Stelle dashes off ahead. Mydei feels a bit like he's walking a particularly rambunctious dog. Mydei and ███████ trail slowly behind her, just far enough that Stelle can do as she pleases, but close enough to keep the property damage to a minimum.

"We'll be okay." ███████ whispers, continuing the conversation from earlier. He tips his head towards Mydei. "I have faith in the Flamechase Journey." He smiles. "And more importantly, I have faith in us."

"Arrogant." Mydei huffs. "That's the sappiest thing I've ever heard you say." He reaches over and flicks ███████ on the forehead. ███████ laughs. It's a bright sound. The light of the Dawn Device is warm against Mydei's skin, and everything about the present feels beautiful.

"We'll be okay." Mydei parrots. He lowers his hand and slings an arm around ███████'s shoulders, pulling the other man towards himself.

"We'll protect everyone." ███████ adds on. "Because that's what we do best."

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.html:
"What was Aedes Elysiae like?" Mydei asks, the next time he see Cyrene.

The two of them sit on the rooftops of the Marmoreal palace. Cyrene swings her legs back and forth off the edge of the gutters.

"Aedes Elysiae?" Cyrene repeats. She tilts her head to the side, a finger coming up to touch her chin. "Why?"

"I'm curious." Mydei says. "I asked Stelle, and she couldn't say much at all."

Cyrene hums. "She never really called that place home like I do." She glances down into the busy streets below their feet. "It's no wonder she can barely remember anything at all." She closes her eyes, leaning forward. For a second, Mydei thinks she might tip off of the roof and into the streets below.

"It was golden." Cyrene continues, eyes still closed. She has a small, fond, smile on her face. "Wheat as far as the eye could see. The leaves were orange and yellow year-round. Sometimes even the sky was gold."

"What were the people like?" Mydei glances down into the street from over Cyrene's shoulder; a group of children trample over a poor lady's flower box as they tear through the streets below. It makes for a lively scene.

"Lovely." Cyrene says. "They were family." She pauses before continuing. "Dad was a farmer. Mom was a tailor. We all went to school together because there were only seven of us in total. Galba would go out hunting and sometimes bring back treats." There's wistfulness in her tone, but her voice lacks its usual floating lilt. "We used to sneak out to the river in the mornings and go fishing together. Well," She pauses, snorting. "He'd go fishing and I'd try to not fall asleep in the mud."

For a moment, she actually looks human. Like the memories are dragging Cyrene from the clouds she's usually in, tying her to the earth and for once, anchoring her down beside Mydei. She opens her eyes; there's a wistful smile painted on her face. She turns that expression towards Mydeimos. "What about your people?"

Mydei blinks. He turns towards Cyrene with a look, motioning vaguely towards a group of Kremnoans circling around the forges.

Cyrene just giggles. "That's not what I meant, silly."

Mydei lowers his arm. "I can't remember my mother." Mydei answers slowly. "But I think she was kind. My father was a bastard through and through."

"And your friends?"

"Loyal." He swallows around the lump in his throat that rises at the mere thought of his old company. "We'd watch each other's backs. Get up to the idiotic sort of stuff teenagers get up to unsupervised in the wild."

"Like throwing rocks at bears?"

Mydei snorts. "Like throwing rocks at bears." He huffs out a breath. "Someone would piss off a guard or a monster and the rest of us would rally behind him and fight it off."

"That's the best sort of riends." Cyrene laughs. "Mine was like that too." She's started rocking back and forth in place, her arms wrapped around herself in a facsimile of a hug. "The kind that you can trust with everything." She curls her fingers, digging her nails into her arms. Mydei hesitates, hands stiff at his sides, wondering if he should try to pry Cyrene's hands open and away from her own skin.

"I don't like thinking back on it too much." Cyrene says, voice all of a sudden soft. "I have my memories of my home, and they are precious to me, but if I spend too long remembering then I'm just going to end up trapped."

"It's still good to remember, though."Mydei says. "At least you have good memories of your home." He can't help but lit a bit of bitterness bleed through into his words on the final statement. What he wouldn't give to have fond memories of Castrum Kremnos. He'd barely had the chance to introduce himself to the city before everything went to hell, let alone form any positive memories beyond the city's association with his father.

Cyrene finally uncurls her arms from around herself and looks up at Mydei. "There's no point in someone like me holding on to those memories, though."

"Someone like you?" Mydei can't help but ask. "Aedes Elysiae was your entire childhood. It is natural to miss it. Right, even."

Cyrene just hums. She taps the heels of her feet against the side of the building. "It's different for me." She says. "I've already gone back so many times now. It never changes." She closes her eyes. She isn't smiling anymore, for once. "Nothing ever changed."

"Cyrene…"

Her eyes snap open suddenly, and she splits into her usual sweet smile. "So I've got to tell you all about it now. That way other people can remember for me. I showed Stelle last time, but next time, you should be the one to accompany him and visit everything."

They both know who the 'him' Cyrene speaks of is, even if Mydei can not recall his name, let alone his face. He already knows that Cyrene knows more than she ever lets on- it's written everywhere in her figure. But sometimes, Mydei can't help but wonder if she's just more than anyone else he's ever known.

"That'd be nice." Mydei acquiesces, even though Aedes Elysiae is already long but ash and memory.

"Don't look so sad." Cyrene smiles. "I'll make sure you'll be able to visit." She leans towards Mydei reaching her hand towards him. Her palm stops just a fraction of a centimeter away from his skin. "Why, we'll even show you around personally."

"Is that really so surprising?" ███████ asks. "Mydeimos, I would do anything for you."

"You wouldn't damn the world." Mydei says easily. "I know you, ███████. You'd damn yourself for me. But at the end of the day you are a hero through and through."

███████ closes his eyes. He leans into Mydei, pressing his face against Mydei's stomach. Mydei runs a hand through ███████'s hair.

"Promise me you'll look after yourself, if you want to do something for me?" Mydei asks softly. His fingers catch an a knot in ███████'s hair. ███████ just wraps his arms around Mydei's waist and squeezes. ███████ doesn't respond, an answer in and of itself. Mydeimos closes his eyes. He leans downard, face hovering just above ███████. He doesn't move any further.

Perhaps he should have.

Okhema falls suddenly, and it falls loudly. Flames eat away at the infrastructure. Civilians run, screaming and sobbing. Even the soldiers are falling.

It's not as if Mydei hadn't expected it; he'd certainly hoped that this day would never come, but it was obvious to anyone with eyes that they were losing the war with the Black Tide. Perhaps there was something he could've done to stall this disaster, but everyone knew that it had not been a matter of if but rather when.

It's worse than the fall of Castrum Kremnos. At least back then, there'd at least been solace in the fact that the survivors would be able to flee to Okhema. Now? There's nowhere left to go. They're a bunch of prey, backed away into a corner with nowhere left to run.

Aglaea is dead, her corpse cooling against the stone on the opposite side of the city. Cipher hasn't been seen in weeks, but if the city's in the state it is now, then she must have fallen too.

███████ is nowhere to be found.

There's a niggling voice in the back of his mind, asking what he's fighting for anymore. Okhema is falling. Okhema will fall. Their last stronghold is meeting its end. The black tide will consume them all- so what's the point of resisting?

He ignores it. He'd never been one to give up in the face of impossibility. Perhaps a miracle will grace them. Perhaps they'll simply get lucky. Better to have tried and failed then to have never tried at all, he tells himself.

He still can't find ███████. Mydeimos tries his best not to worry. ███████ can handle himself. He has to.

As if on cue, a flash of white and silver catches Mydei's eye. He looks up from his fight. ███████ meets his gaze from across the battlefield. Mydei doesn't know how long he's been fighting. He thinks he might've died more times in this singular battle than he has in the past decade. It's just an endless stream of black tide monsters, now. Mydei's not even sure if there are any civilians left in Okhema for him to protect. But ███████ is still there, and that's something that counts for itself.

He throws the corpse of a tide-eroded blade off of him, the movement strained with effort. There's mud and blood and sludge piling at his feet, a horrid mimicry of the sea. But ███████ is just over there, on the other side of the courtyard, and Mydei has to move towards him.

Like a moth drawn towards the moon. Eagerly and trusting, wanting nothing more than to be close to that wondrous light.

Like a moth drawn towards sun. The flames eat away at fragile wings, and so Icarus falls.

Mydei barely even registers the attack coming. The blade goes easily through his back. Mydei hears the sickening crunch of bone, and he collapses in a heap to the ground, legs going numb beneath him, all sensation disappearing into static.

Mydei has died perhaps millions of times by now. Each death is always slightly different, but the dying itself- that is always the same. He's grown used to the numbing feeling of his soul being dragged down to the sea of souls.

This time though, there's a finality to death.

Ah, Mydei thinks, even as that familiar cold spreads through his body. I didn't mean to die like this. It's a warrior's death, certainly. He's dying in service of the Flamechase. It is an honorable death. With glory.

But ███████'s expression is a wretched, broken thing. Mydei doesn't want to see it. He'd never wanted to see it.

Sorry, Mydei wants to say, even though his lungs are running out of air. I didn't want to hurt you like this. I didn't want you to see. He's so close to Mydei, but Mydei won't ever be able to reach him. The blade is yanked unceremoniously from his back, but Mydei can't even feel at anymore.

Mydei's senses are fading; there's black creeping in from the edges of his vision- his limbs are going numb, but he can still see the way ███████'s chest heaves. He can faintly hear ███████ scream out- in rage, perhaps, or grief, or a combination of both.

That wound in Mydei's back bleeds sluggishly. He is so, so, tired. He wants to rest. He doesn't want to leave yet. ███████ cries and cries, and Mydei can not last.

Mydeimos the undying lets his eyes finally slip shut as he lets out one last tired breath. His executioner takes another step forward.

Chapter End Notes
