chapters.title: Chapter 7
chapters.html:
He's had these dreams for as long as he could remember- these otherworldly sort of dreams, where he dreams of a childhood he never had, but perhaps could have had in another life. He dreams of golden fields and bright red cities and vibrant blue skies. A father who raises him and shows him how to hunt. A mother who holds him close and teaches him to fight. White hair and blue eyes and love, love, love, love, love.

Every time without fail, he wakes up grieving for something he'd never had.

This time, the dreams feel startlingly different. For one, Stelle features in them, something that had never happened before.

The outlander is stacking some sleeping chimeras on top of the Tribbies' desk. That white-haired figure with a face that Mydei can never see properly is muffling his giggles into his hand right alongside her.

"Deliverer." Mydei scolds. He doesn't know who he intends to call out too, but his eyes slide automatically to Stelle; he never could fully focus on that white-haired figure, even in dreams like this one.

Stelle makes a disgusted noise. "Who're you calling Deliverer? 'Vili's sake it makes it sound like you're cheating on him with me or something."

"Are you cheating on me?" The white-haired figure splays their hand across their chest in mock offense. "Mydei, darling, love of my life, I'm hurt." Stelle bursts out laughing, and the white-haired figure laughs alongside her.

The dreams shifts, warps and goes sideways and all of a sudden it's just Mydei and Stelle standing in empty Okhema streets. The sky is darkening above their heads in a way that it never should be, for Okhema.

Stelle looks Mydei in the eyes. She smirks, but the smile doesn't reach her eyes. "Who're you calling Deliverer?" She repeats. "Save that for him when he comes back."

"For who?" Mydeimos asks, like he always does when faced with the idea of that lovely, nameless hero.

"You know already know who." Stelle laughs. Her skin flakes away from her body in pale chips. Gold bleeds from underneath her skin. There are hands grabbing at Mydei's ankles and all of a sudden he feels like he can't breathe. "How could you ever forget him?" She reaches up towards Mydei, tips his head towards the ground.

He's no longer in Okhema anymore. He's standing in a pool of golden blood. Thousands (millions?) of dead blue eyes stare up at him, a pair to match each cold cracked body.

There's no end to the bodies.

The Black Tide has been getting worse recently. The Grove's just fallen. Even Stelle, for all her exuberance, can not find the energy to joke and laugh around in these times.

Mydei should be in the war rooms, drawing up defense plans with Aglaea and the others. Instead he's sitting in a cafe across from Stelle as the pair of them listlessly poke at the flat honeycakes on their plates.

He thinks he knows why he's here instead. There's a particular sense of comradery, in being the only people who can remember even a snippet of all those previous lives. All they'd need now is Cyrene and the three of them would make a rather tragic trio.

"I have these dreams," Mydei starts. "Where my mother raises me."

Stelle looks at him strangely. She doesn't say a word.

Mydei continues on. "I'd thought those false memories had faded, after I'd returned to Castrum Kremnos, but ever since I arrived at Okhema, there would be other dreams. I spar with someone on the rooftops. We compete over who can last the longest in the bath's. We visit the chimeras together. We go almost everywhere together."

Stelle closes her eyes. Her expression looks pained.

"You refuse to spar with me." Mydei says. "Our relationship could be described a close coworkers, perhaps even friends, but we do not spend every waking moment together.

"You bear the role of Deliverer." Mydei continues, and his throat closes around the name again. "You refuse to let me call you by that title."

"You don't want to call me by that name, either." Stelle finally speaks up. She opens her eyes and turns her gaze towards Mydei. Her eyes are a shade of piercing gold, and it's all wrong. The Deliverer's eyes should be blue- "We both know that name doesn't belong to me."

"Doesn't it?" Wrong, wrong, this is all wrong. There are overlapping images flashing across Mydei's vision. The heir of worldbearing has grey hair and gold eyes. The heir of worldbearing has white hair and blue eyes. Mydei misses him so terribly.

"Mydei," Stelle says. Her voice is unusually soft. She looks like she's about to cry. Mydei feels like he's about to cry. "Who are you remembering? Can you say his name, at the very least?"

"I don't know." Mydei says. "How can I remember someone I've never met?"

"You remember your mother." Stelle's hands come up to grip Mydei by the forearms. She squeezes him with a surprising amount of force. "You never met her either."

"Can't you give me his name?" Mydei tries weakly.

"███████." Stelle whispers. "███████. ███████." She shakes her head. The syllables come out jumbled and warped. They're static in Mydei's ears.

"I'm sorry," She finally releases Mydei and takes a step back. "I know how important he was to you, but you're going to have to remember for yourself."

"I'm trying." Mydei's voice cracks.

"I know you are." Stelle's voice is soft. "It isn't enough."

He knows who he's trying to remember. He's slowly remembering him already- why else would he hurt this much? He wants so badly to remember. The not knowing is breaking his heart.

But the knowing would break his heart too. He already finds himself turning to empty spaces and setting aside treats for someone who does not exist.

What is worse? To have forgotten that is not here, or to remember the missing and spend the rest of time longing for that which is gone?

"I miss him." Mydei says quietly.

"I know." Stelle responds. "I do too."

There is a white-haired man standing on the other side of the scales.

"I hope you still remember your purpose, new recruit." Mydei says lowly, crossing his arms in front of his chest.

"You seem awfully confident, Kremnoan." The white-haired man grins back, all sharp canines and casual confidence. "Let's see how you define the idea of weight."

His mother's signet ring has never been heavier in the palm of Mydei's hand. He strides forward, places it in the center of his scale. For Glory, his people would say. For the people, his mother would say.

"A ring?" The white-haired man asks, tone lilting upward. "Is there a story here?"

"Nothing I'd spill to you." Mydeimos bites out. He steps off of the scale, taking his original position. "Just know that Castrum Kremnos' glory could bring a titan to its knees, let alone someone like you."

Mydeimos can't quite see the white-haired man's expression from here, but he thinks the other man might be smiling. The white-haired man turns to Cyrene, who's standing beside him with her hands folded behind her back. They exchange a few words, and the soldier steps forward again, this time with what looks to be a piece of paper in his hand.

Cyrene catches Mydei's eye as the soldier steps forward. She winks at him, smiling. Mydei tears his gaze away.

"Something that weighs more than the fate of the world," The man says, as he sets down the paper- the card- down on the scale, "is the resolve to shoulder an unchangeable past, and carry it into the future." He looks up, gaze matching Mydeimos'. Golden on blue. A king and his living. A soldier and his dead. The white-haired man steps off of the scales, and Talanton make its judgment.

The scale is perfectly balanced.

The weight of the future, Mydeimos thinks, versus the weight of the past. Funny, how things seemed to have worked out like that. The figure across from him certainly isn't without his own ghosts. Perhaps Mydei would be the same, if he didn't have an entire nation's worth of people depending on him.

"Placing us both on the same side of the scale?" Mydei says disparagingly. "Such weak idealism will only get you skewered on spears."

"Fine by me." The white-haired man laughs, kneeling down to peel the card from the ground. "I never claimed to be that Deliverer from that card, you know?"

"And yet here you are, touting on about saving my people too."

"Just because we're from different cities doesn't mean that the Black Tide will spare us." The soldier replies easily, rising to his full height. "Even from this exchange alone, I can tell that you're someone who will fight for the weak, all while dressing up that effort in the name of glory. In a way we're the same when it comes to some so-called heroism. Carrying the weight of the world on your shoulders. You have people you need to protect. A city to save. "

"And yet you've chosen to carry this all onto your own two shoulders." Mydei answers. "Including my people."

The soldier falls silent for a moment. The pink-haired girl beside him frowns, reaching forward to tug on his sleeve. After a moment, the soldier finally speaks again.

"I don't think I'll be alone for it." He says slowly. "But as an heir. As a soldier, or a fighter, or just someone who's survived the Black Tide, I think it's simply my duty. We're capable of surviving, so is it not up to us to ensure that others can live as well?"

Mydeimos huffs. "It seems to me as if you really are trying to claim to be the Deliverer in that card." The man just smiles in response. There's a tinge of something sad, to it. Mydei lets out a breath, steps forward onto the scale, and retrieves his mother's signet ring.

Lady Aglaea and Tribios say some pleasantries, on the purpose of the Flame Chase. The glory, the honor, the importance. Mydeimos only listens with half an ear. He turns the signet ring over and over in his hand, the metal clinking against his gauntlets. Cyrene's still staring at him from across the hall, eyes dark with intent. Intent for what, Mydei couldn't name; he doesn't know here near well enough.

Eventually, their talks come to an end. The white-haired soldier slips his card into his coat, and Mydei slips his mother's ring into the folds of his own robes.

"I shall see you in Okhema, Deliverer." He says, finally meeting the Deliverer's gaze.

Phainon grins, wide and blinding. He looks terribly alive, especially amongst the rubble of this old, abandoned city.

"And you, Mydeimos."

Deliverer was the only thing Mydei ever called him, afterwards.

Sometimes he wondered if he should've called out his real name more instead.

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.html:
Mydeimos isn't exactly present for the finale- had died when Okhema fell, this time around. He spends some indeterminate amount of time whirling around in what feels like a pool of cool jelly. The few times he manages to peel open his eyes, it's to a whirlpool of ever shifting colors, lights that almost look like stars, and a pounding headache.

Eventually, things settle down, a the feeling of breaking out from beneath a surface of water washes over Mydei. When he opens his eyes this time, his surroundings have settled into something approaching a starry night sky. There's splashes of pinks and purples hanging overhead, a view that's most certainly not native to Amphoreus. He curls his hands into a fist, feeling his fingers sink into the jelly-like consistency of the floor beneath him.

He sits up, glancing around. There's not another soul in sight.

"Hello?" He calls out anyway. Slowly, he pushes himself up to his feet. Despite being thrown around, stabbed, fought his way through apocalypse- nothing hurts. Even the headache from earlier is nothing more than a memory of sensation. Mydeimos stands in place for a few moments, tensely clenching and unclenching his fists, glancing around the endless expanse of the space around him.

Eventually, he gives up on trying to figure out where he is. Just randomly picks a direction and heads off in that direction.

With no reference point, no horizon in sight, it's almost as if he's stuck walking in place. His body tells him he's moving forward, his eyes tell that he's getting nowhere. His steps eventually slow, and he pauses again, staring into some distance point in this confusing space.

"Hi~" A familiar voice calls out in singsong.

Mydei whirls around, hands instinctively coming up to brace. Cyrene- or Mydei thinks she's Cyrene- giggles, and wiggles her fingers at Mydei in a wave.

She's much taller now, almost around Cipher's height, if Mydei had to guess. She's dressed in a white flowy dress, the style unfamiliar to Mydei.

"Cyrene." Mydei says dumbly. "What are you doing here?"

Cyrene just smiles even wider. She leans forward, taking one of Mydei's hands within her own, and begins pulling him off in a direction. Mydei only hesitates for a moment, before letting the shorter girl lead.

"I should be the one asking you that." Cyrene doesn't look back at Mydei. She picks up speed, bouncing forward with the stride one would expect from a prancing deer; Mydei has to break into a light jog to keep up with her. "I didn't think anyone but the outworlders, and maybe Phainon, would ever find their way here." She breaks into a laugh in the middle. "But, well, you've always defied expectations too, Mydeimos. You and Phainon really are well suited for one another."

"Phainon-" Mydeimos latches on the name- and look at that, he can actually say the name now, without stumbling on syllables and half-remember tones. "Is he here too?"

"He went on ahead." Cyrene answers easily. She tugs on Mydei's arm a bit harder. The stars around them finally start to blur with motion. "Don't worry. You'll catch up to him soon."

Something about her wording rankles Mydei. "What about you?" He can't help but ask. "Or Stelle?"

"Stelle went back to the Astral Express." Cyrene blithely answers. "That's her home, after all."

"What about you, Cyrene."

The pink-haired girl falls silent at that. The stars have started dropping from the sky around them, sinking down in streaks, like raindrops running down the sides of metal blades.

"Cyrene." Mydei repeats. He digs his heels into the ground, slowing them to a near stop. The stars whirl around them. "What about you."

Cyrene is silent for a moment. Finally, she glances back over her shoulder, making eye contact with Mydei. She's smiling, but there's something wretched to her expression.

"You remember his name now, right?" Cyrene asks, still smiling. Still looking like she's trying not to cry.

"Phainon." Mydei says. "Deliverer." His comrade, best friend, lover, soulmate. His world- there are not enough words for them, not in the Kremnoan dictionary, nor in the Okheman.

"Yes." Cyrene's eyes crinkle when she smiles. "Phainon of Aedes Elysiae." She twirls around in a circle as she says the name; her skirt billows out around her. She twists into a skip and approaches Mydei with a bounce in her step.

"You and Phainon are really good for each other." She says.

"Cyrene."

She draws in a breath. The stars blur, colors melting into one another, lighting up the space in a bright white light.

When the light fades, they're standing on a dock. There's a golden sunset overhead, a golden sun reflected in the sea, and a golden field at their feet.

Cyrene laughs. "Didn't you notice?" She clasps her hands behind her back and leans down to look up at Mydei through her eyelashes. "How I never spoke to anyone but you and Stelle?"

Mydei has a feeling on where this is going. He doesn't like it all.

"How did you know my name?" Cyrene continues. "I never introduced myself to you. Neither did Stelle."

"Those other memories." Mydei finally manages to say.

Cyrene stands back upright. She tilts her head to the side, still smiling. "Those other memories." She parrots. "But what about everything else?" She reaches upward, lightly patting Mydeimos on the shoulder. "You, Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos, have always been an anomaly amongst the heirs. Your powers do not match your path. You, well, borrowed, to put it nicely, some of Castorice's authority. Memories of previous cycles kept on bleeding into your mind. Any more than that, and perhaps you would've ended up as an existence like Phainon and myself. Someone who stepped out of their own story. It was quite fascinating to watch, actually." She plops down on the edge of the pier, swinging her legs over the water. Her heels dangle from her toes as she flexes her feet. Mydei watches her for a few quiet moments, then joins her by the water.

"Were you ever really here at all?" He asks quietly.

"Once upon a time," She closes her eyes. "I just left everything behind a bit before everyone else, that's all. Reached my ending before this chapter even started, if you want to look at it like that."

The fall into silence again. Cyrene starts humming, a soft, slow tune. Mydei thinks he might've heard Phainon humming it too, once upon a time. Perhaps its a folk song from Aedes Elysiae, lost like everything else to the seas of time and the grasp of the Black Tide.

"You're still alive, right?" Cyrene suddenly asks. "It's a bit hard to tell, in this place. I haven't been able to see things in the real world properly for a long time."

"I am." Mydei asnwers. "Or at least I think so."

"That's good enough." Cyrene laughs. "If you believe you are alive, then you are. And that means that all the others shall join you too." She reaches into one of the folds in her dress, pulling out her stack of tarot cards from thin air. The Deliverer card seems to burn against Mydei's skin, from the spot where it's pressed against his chest.

Cyrene leans to the side, holding out the deck of cards. When Mydei doesn't raise his arms to take them, she pushes the stack of cards against Mydei's chest. She loosens her grip, and the cards start to fall; Mydei's hands instinctively come up to clutch at the deck.

"I'm not afraid of dying." She says. "It's been such a long time that I think a little bit of a rest would be nice." She's still smiling, but her eyes are starting to glisten with tears again. "But it'd be nice to be remembered, I think."

"I'll pass them on to him." Mydei says, his mouth dry, already knowing Cyrene's request before she can so much as put it into words.

"Thank you." Cyrene says. Her eyes dip down to the floor, to the sky reflected beneath their feet. "I'm really glad I got to properly meet you, this time. I wished that three of us could've all hung out together. Run around in the wheat fields. Get lost in the Membrance Maze, but I don't think that'll possible."

She looks back up at Mydei and smiles. Her tears have fallen free, running in glistening trails down her face. "Look after him for me? He's a bit of a reckless idiot."

"I will." Mydei swears. "I promise."

"Good." Cyrene says through her tears. She's laughing, even as she chokes on her own tears. "At least one of us should be there for him at the end."

And with that, with far more strength than one would expect from a girl of her size, Cyrene tugs Mydeimos off of the pier, plunging him into the ocean water below.

Mydei is floating. He thinks he's still alive, but it doesn't feel like it. He can't feel his limbs. He can't feel his body at all. It feels like floating in the sea, or trudging through the waters around Styxia. All the strength seeping from his bones.

But his heart is pounding in his ears, and the dead do not have heartbeats.

Time passes. Perhaps it is only moments. Perhaps it is eons.

The next time he opens his eyes, it is to sand beneath his fingertips, and blue, wideyed-gaze staring down at him from overhead.

"Deliverer?" Mydei rasps out. "Phainon?"

Phainon's expression goes surprised, just for the briefest of moments, before he splits into a blinding smile. He glows like the sun. He's beautiful. Mydei has never seen anything more grand.

"Mydei," Phainon says. His eyes glisten with tears, and Mydei can feel his own eyes burning. He pushes himself out of the water, towards Phainon, and throws his arms across Phainon's shoulders.

"Deliverer." Mydei chokes out. He squeezes his eyes shut as his tears mix with the sea water still stuck to his skin. "Phainon." Incredulous laughter bubbles out of him, and he laughs and laughs, muffling his mirth into Phainon's skin.

"Mydei." Phainon laughs. It's a wet laugh, and he squeezes Mydei back. "Hi. I'm sorry it took me so long."

"Phainon." Mydei's started sobbing now. He buries his face into the crook of Phainon's neck, digging his fingers into Phainon's back. Presses closed-mouth kisses against Phainon's skin. "You damn bastard."

"'M Sorry." Phainon lets out another choked laugh. He presses a kiss against the side of Mydei's head and runs his hand along Mydei's spine. "I didn't want to hurt you. I didn't think that you'd remember."

"How could I possibly forget you?" Mydei could hit Phainon right now, but he's too busy sinking into the warmth of Phainon's body. Phainon smells of the sun and sea and sweat. It's honestly a bit gross, but Mydei basks in it anyway. It's proof that they're both alive. Here. Present enough to feel and prod it and be disgusted and be happy with and everything he'd ever dreamed off.

Phainon presses against Mydei's body like his trying to sink into him, as if by pressing close enough, their limbs could fuse, and they'd never have to part again. Mydeimos presses back. When Phainon leans back, falling to the sand, he pulls Mydei down on with him. Their legs tangle together as they lie there on the shore.

There's no other sound on this shore, except for the mix of their laughter and sobs, and the gentle roar of ocean waves. Phainon rubs his hand along Mydei's back in a soothing motion. Mydeimos clings to Phainon like he's his lifelinfe. Eventually, they calm, and they're just two men lying on a beach, rather than two lovers who haven't seen each other in centuries.

"I saw Cyrene." Mydei mumbles. Phainon's hand pauses in its ministrations.

"Yeah?"

"She was really nice." Mydei rolls over onto the side to lay beside Phainon. He presses his body up against the Deliverer's. "A little bit creepy, but really sweet."

Phainon snorts. "She was saying all sorts of all-knowing stuff again, wasn't she?" He snickers. "Yeah, she can get like that sometimes."

Mydei hums. "We'd go to the garden of life and play with the chimeras together all the time."

Phainon's expression falls a little at that. "I did want to show her. It was only back in that first cycle that she'd ever made it to Okhema, and by that point things were so bad we didn't have the time."

"She really liked the chimeras."

"I'd thought that she would." Phainon reaches over to clasp Mydei's hand in his. Mydei squeezes right back. He reaches into his robes with his free hand. Pulls free the tarot cards that Cyrene had gifted them.

Phainon takes them with his free hand. He holds them up above his head, the cards casting a long shadow over his eyes. He lets out a breath, squeezes Mydei's hand again, and stows the cards in his own coat.

"I'll hold on to the Deliverer card." Mydeimos says. "It was one of the first things that made me remember you."

"That's alright." Phainon breathlessly laughs. "I think Cyrene would've wanted you to keep that one anyway." He holds a hand over his heart, pressing against his chest over the place where he's tucked the cards away.

"Are the others here?" Phainon asks.

"Yeah." Mydei says. "You succeeded. Don't worry."

Phainon lets out a wet laugh. "Do you think they remember?"

"Who knows?" Mydei lets his eyes fall shut. "We remember, after all."
